001: Ivan, have you already received the plan for tomorrow's exhibition? We need to divide up the responsibilities.
Yes, Anna, I was just looking it over. I think I should stay at the booth, and you could handle negotiations with potential partners.
Agreed, that makes sense. But I'll need your support if technical questions about the product come up.
Of course, I'll be available. By the way, our booth will be located in the central hall, which is a very good spot.
Great, that will increase our foot traffic. I'll prepare some brief presentation materials by morning.
Perfect. Then let's meet tomorrow at eight in the morning at the main entrance so we have time to get everything ready.
002: Dmitry, what did you think of yesterday's international trade fair? Was it worth going there?
Honestly, Anna, the impressions are mixed. Competitors presented some very strong developments, but we also have clear advantages.
Like what exactly? I need to understand what to focus on in the report for management.
Our product is significantly easier to use, and many visitors pointed that out. Plus, the price turned out to be more attractive.
Those are good points. Were there any actual orders, or just interest?
We collected contacts from three serious companies; they want to run test trials. That's already a decent result.
003: Sergey, look at how long the line is at our booth. It seems the presentation of the new model caused quite a stir.
Yes, Elena, I didn't even expect such a crowd. We'll have to ask the administration to issue additional passes for tomorrow.
I've already contacted the organizers, and they promised to sort it out. But we need to figure out how to handle this many visitors.
I think we should split the flow: I'll do the demonstrations, and you'll answer questions and collect inquiries.
Makes sense. Just don't forget that we have a meeting with the press scheduled at three o'clock.
I remember, I've prepared a press release for them. I hope we manage to draw some extra attention to our booth.
004: Ivan, have you seen where they put the catalogs from our booth? They ran out by lunchtime.
I noticed they went fast. I ordered an additional print run, but it won't arrive until tomorrow morning.
That's a problem. Without catalogs, it'll be hard to keep visitors' attention. Maybe we can offer them the electronic version?
Great idea. I've prepared a QR code with a link to our website; we can print it on business cards.
Let's do that. And we also need to think about how we'll collect contacts if the paper forms run out too.
I'll set up a special registration form on the tablet. It's actually more convenient; the data goes straight into the database.
005: Elena, how did the negotiations with the company from Kazakhstan go? I saw you were talking with them at our booth for a long time.
Very productive, Sergey. They're interested in long-term cooperation, but they want a discount for a wholesale purchase.
That's good news. What volume are they ready to buy at first?
We're talking about a fairly large batch, so I promised to discuss the terms with management. We need to prepare a commercial proposal.
I'll take care of that this evening. Maybe we should offer them free delivery to seal the deal?
That would be reasonable. If we give in on delivery, we can keep the price at the level we want.
006: Dmitry, have you noticed that the competitors keep taking pictures of our booth? It's starting to worry me.
I've seen it too, Anna. They're clearly studying our new development. We need to be more careful with the details.
Maybe we should take the technical documentation off the booth and leave only the general brochures?
Agreed, that's the right call. We especially shouldn't show the drawings and specifications; that's our intellectual property.
I'll make sure everything gets put away for the rest of the exhibition. And I'll ask security to keep an eye on this booth.
Good. And I also advise not discussing technical details in the common areas; there might be too many extra ears there.
007: Sergey, the organizers are offering us to hold a workshop tomorrow in the afternoon. What do you think about that?
That's a great opportunity to make a name for ourselves, Elena. But we need to quickly prepare the program and materials.
I've already sketched out a rough plan: we'll show our product in action and talk about its advantages over competitors.
Sounds good. We just need to figure out who will lead the workshop and how we'll attract enough participants.
I could take on the main part, and you can help with the equipment demonstration. We'll announce the workshop over the loudspeaker.
Deal. I'll prepare the presentation and make sure all the equipment works without any glitches.
008: Ivan, did you hear the news? Our booth was mentioned in the official exhibition review as one of the most interesting.
Really? That's great news, Anna! A mention like that could bring us even more visitors.
That's exactly why I'm suggesting we strengthen our team for tomorrow. Maybe we should bring in one more employee from the office.
I already called Alexei; he's ready to come and help. He knows the product well and is good with clients.
Perfect. Then I'll prepare a brief guide for him and introduce him to the key visitors we've already spoken with.
Great. With that kind of support, we'll be able to reach a lot more interested companies.
009: Elena, how did you manage to arrange a joint booth with the company from Novosibirsk? I thought they had already left.
We met with their representative at a cafe, and he showed interest in our proposal. They're staying until the exhibition closes.
That's wonderful! A joint booth will let us present a more complete solution to clients.
Exactly. They're offering additional equipment, and we're providing the software. Together, it looks very convincing.
We'll need to prepare a joint presentation and agree on how to split the rental costs.
I already discussed it with them; they agree to split the costs evenly. We just need to finalize the design details.
010: Dmitry, the exhibition is coming to an end, and we need to sum things up. How many contacts have we collected over these days?
I counted more than a hundred and fifty interested companies, Anna. That's significantly more than we expected.
An impressive result. Now the main thing is to process these contacts properly and not lose a single potential client.
I suggest we hold a meeting tomorrow and distribute all the inquiries among the sales managers.
Agreed. And we need to prepare thank-you letters for everyone who visited our booth; it will increase loyalty.
Great idea. I'll take care of that right after we take down the booth and pack up the equipment.
